children: Cyabra said it entered a six-figure annual agreement with an interactive entertainment and gaming company.
Under the agreement, Cyabra would monitor social and digital environments, analyzing authenticity and identifying coordinated or inauthentic activity, the company said Friday.

Cyabra--which uses artificial intelligence to work with governments and enterprises to detect coordinated manipulation--said the contract is part of its expansion into the private sector, and shows its ability to scale its technology and services across large digital communities.

"Coordinated manipulation can distort how organizations understand what their audiences actually think," Chief Executive Dan Brahmy said. "Gaming is one of the most consequential and increasingly important environments for this kind of activity. Review manipulation, orchestrated campaigns, and amplified narratives can shape how a title is received and how a community experiences it."
